description: Example queries of the SQL page; scripts/test_visitor_products.py runs each one with DuckDB against the deploy's tables.

examples.title: CTAS classifications
examples.sql:
SELECT classification, count(*) AS n
FROM ctas_candidates
GROUP BY classification
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 20

examples.title: Bright type Ia supernovae
examples.sql:
SELECT name, discovery_time, discovery_magnitude, redshift
FROM ctas_candidates
WHERE classification LIKE 'SN Ia%' AND discovery_magnitude < 17
ORDER BY discovery_time DESC
LIMIT 50

examples.title: CTAS events per survey and month
examples.sql:
SELECT discovery_survey, substr(discovery_time, 1, 7) AS month, count(*) AS n
FROM ctas_candidates
WHERE discovery_time >= '2026-01'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY month DESC, n DESC
LIMIT 60

examples.title: Planets by method and decade
examples.sql:
SELECT method_code, (discovery_year // 10) * 10 AS decade, count(*) AS n
FROM worldsindex_objects
WHERE status = 'CONFIRMED' AND discovery_year IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY decade, n DESC

examples.title: Temperate small planets
examples.sql:
SELECT name, host_name, radius_earth, insolation_earth, equilibrium_temperature_k
FROM worldsindex_objects
WHERE status = 'CONFIRMED' AND radius_earth < 1.8 AND insolation_earth BETWEEN 0.3 AND 1.7
ORDER BY insolation_earth

examples.title: Catalogs that disagree on a period
examples.sql:
SELECT name, count(DISTINCT source_id) AS catalogs, min(value) AS shortest, max(value) AS longest
FROM worldsindex_measurements
WHERE property_code = 'orbital_period'
GROUP BY name
HAVING catalogs > 1 AND max(value) > 1.01 * min(value)
ORDER BY longest / shortest DESC
LIMIT 30

examples.title: Bright transit hosts
examples.sql:
SELECT name, period_days, depth_ppt, host_mag, host_mag_band
FROM worldsindex_transit_ephemerides
WHERE host_mag < 10 AND depth_ppt > 5
ORDER BY host_mag
LIMIT 40

examples.title: Cone around M 101
examples.sql:
SELECT name, classification, discovery_time, ra_deg, dec_deg
FROM ctas_candidates
WHERE 2 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(dec_deg - 54.3489) / 2), 2) + cos(radians(dec_deg)) * cos(radians(54.3489)) * pow(sin(radians(ra_deg - 210.8023) / 2), 2))) < radians(0.5)
